answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable chain of sequential modular squarings before it is accepted. Because each squaring depends on the previous result, GPUs cannot parallelize one clone’s evaluation to shorten its elapsed time; they can only run separate clones concurrently, each paying its own time cost. A garden of saffron and onyx identities therefore faces a physical bottleneck proportional to the number of proofs.
